findings.location: source.html paragraph 3 ("As we cross the equinox...")
findings.source_quote: As we cross the equinox, “the days get longer, and winter gets stronger”, states the old proverb, and it remains incisively correct.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate or localize “equinox” into standard Afrikaans (do not leave the English word). For example: replace the phrase with: "Soos ons die gelyklop oorsteek, sê die ou spreekwoord: 'die dae word langer, en die winter word sterker,' en dit bly skerp korrek." Preserve the existing HTML and punctuation.
findings.translation_quote: Soos ons die equinox oorsteek, stel die ou spreekwoord dat “die dae langer word, en die winter sterker raak”, en dit bly skerp korrek.

findings.location: source.html paragraph 4 ("Northern tradition states that the robins...")
findings.source_quote: Northern tradition states that the robins must get snowed on three times before the full arrival of spring.
findings.suggested_fix: The translator rendered "robins" as "swartbosvinke", which is a different bird-name and can mislead readers. Use a standard Afrikaans name for "robins" (for example "rooiborsvoëls" or simply "robins" transliterated if preferred by the publication) so the meaning of the proverb is preserved. Suggested replacement: "Noordelike tradisie sê dat die robins (rooiborsvoëls) drie keer in die sneeu moet beland voordat die lente volkome aankom." Preserve HTML and punctuation.
findings.translation_quote: Noordelike tradisie sê dat die swartebosvinke drie keer in die sneeu moet beland voordat die lente volkome aankom.
